overview: DR Congo's women's health innovation ecosystem is anchored less in venture-backed femtech startups than in government maternal-health reform and donor-funded digital and logistics programs. The state is rolling out free maternity care as the first tier of Universal Health Coverage, now live in 14 of 26 provinces, alongside a landmark national contraceptive commitment. A small but growing set of local digital-health startups and international partners (UNFPA, Japan, VillageReach, Ipas, drone operators) are layering technology onto antenatal care, reproductive-health information, and cervical-cancer control, mostly in Kinshasa and the conflict-affected east.

sections.heading: Latest major news
sections.narrative: Recent activity clusters around new digital maternal-health platforms and Japan-backed remote diagnostics.

items.text: Kulela, a digital platform to guide pregnant women, parents and families and cut maternal mortality, launched at Silikin Village in Kinshasa.
Congolese startup Lax Medical launched its e-sante platform (online booking, digital medical records, clinic management) in Kinshasa as part of the 2025 Grandir & Faire Grandir cohort.
UNFPA, Japan and SOIK Corporation launched a USD 2M project deploying mobile clinics with SPAQ smart antenatal diagnostics to cut perinatal mortality in Nord-Kivu and Ituri, training 100 midwives.
National Forum for the Elimination of Cervical Cancer held in Kinshasa; national cervical & breast cancer strategy revised for 2024-2029.

sections.heading: Policy & strategy
sections.narrative: Women's health is central to President Tshisekedi's Universal Health Coverage push, delivered as free maternity care plus reproductive-health financing.

items.text: DRC pledged USD 5M/year for contraceptives (2025-2028) at the International Conference on Family Planning in Bogota.
Free maternity care operational in 14 of 26 provinces (257 of 519 health zones); Kinshasa, Kongo Central and Kasai Oriental state-funded, 11 provinces World Bank-funded.
Revised national strategy against cervical and breast cancer (2024-2029) signed by the Health Minister and WHO Africa.
DRC launched its first nationwide HPV vaccination campaign targeting girls aged 9-14 with the quadrivalent vaccine.

sections.heading: Latest ecosystem moves
sections.narrative: Local incubators and digital-health startups in Kinshasa are beginning to intersect with women's health, while donor programs scale reproductive-health tech.

items.text: Silikin Village, a Kinshasa innovation hub, hosted both the Kulela maternal-health platform launch and the Grandir & Faire Grandir startup cohort that includes Lax Medical.

Nurse Nisa, an Ipas WhatsApp chatbot providing confidential SRH information on contraception, abortion, emergency contraception and gender-based violence in English, French and Swahili, operates in DRC (and Kenya).
UNFPA-supported training produced 537 midwife graduates across 12 schools in 7 provinces, with 1.2M additional family-planning users reached in 2024.
Smartphone-based visual cervical inspection screening validated in Kinshasa as a sustainable, internationally monitored system.

sections.narrative: Funding is dominated by government and donor commitments rather than equity rounds, reflecting a program-led ecosystem.

sections.heading: Key players & hubs

items.note: WhatsApp SRH chatbot on contraception, abortion self-management and GBV, active in DRC

items.note: Kinshasa innovation hub hosting the Grandir & Faire Grandir cohort and health-tech launches

items.note: Leads free maternity care under Universal Health Coverage and the cervical/breast cancer strategy
